title: Rollout semaphore expiry triggered divergent variant splits and surge containment
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a scheduled canary promotion for model v2.11.3 we observed a rapid divergence in routing state that resulted in two overlapping A/B splits and a temporary 2x capacity spike on inference backends. Traffic recovery relied on manual isolation and emergency throttles. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and longer-term actions to prevent semaphore/expiry driven split divergence in future rollouts.
impact_summary: ~17 minutes of elevated latencies for 18% of customer requests in us-west-2; no model corruption; one customer reported transient 502s during the surge. Cost impact estimated ~USD 6.2k in excess GPU time for the event window.
timeline: 2026-02-20 09:04 UTC: Canary rollout started for v2.11.3 using rollout controller RC-1221 with target 10% canary
2026-02-20 09:14 UTC: Orchestrator delayed full promotion due to a slow healthcheck; rollout controller acquired semaphore key 'rollout/RC-1221' with 300s TTL
2026-02-20 09:19 UTC: Healthcheck recovered; controller attempted promotion but semaphore TTL had expired while controller was still in mid-state transition

2026-02-20 09:19:05 UTC: A second promotion worker (leader re-election) also attempted changes; absent a valid lock, both workers applied different partial route deltas (one created A/B split 12%->new, the other applied a canary-adjust weight rewrite), producing overlapping routing entries

2026-02-20 09:19-09:36 UTC: Frontend split resolution logic treated overlapping rules as additive under a legacy merge path; overlapping rules sent duplicate requests to backends causing a surge and KV cache invalidations across shards

2026-02-20 09:24 UTC: On-call triage throttled incoming canary traffic and pinned model to previous stable version via emergency route pin; manual eviction of duplicate route fragments performed by infra team
2026-02-20 09:36 UTC: Traffic normalized; monitoring and post-incident checks initiated
2026-02-20 10:05 UTC: Incident declared resolved for customer impact; follow-up investigation tasks created
root_cause: Rollout controller used a semaphore TTL (300s) that expired during a mid-transition step, allowing a leader-change to concurrently apply partial route deltas.
Route merging logic in the edge translator treats overlapping A/B rules as additive rather than conflicting, which allowed duplicate targetting instead of rejecting or reconciling partial updates.
No cross-check in the orchestrator to ensure a change-set is applied atomically across route fragments; partial writes were possible when leadership moved or a controller retried after TTL expiry.
Lack of synthetic gating for concurrent promotions: the canary healthcheck flap duration was within TTL but the controller did not re-validate lock ownership before applying final promotion steps.
short_term_mitigations: Reintroduced emergency route pinning playbook to rapidly freeze traffic to stable model variants (completed during incident).
Lowered default semaphore TTL from 300s to 90s to reduce window for stale leadership drift (rollout config change - staged).
Edge translator change: treat overlapping A/B rule writes as atomic conflict and reject the second writer until reconciliation (hotfix deployed to staging).
Added an orchestrator reconciliation job that scans for duplicated route fragments and collapses overlapping rules (monitor-only for 48h).
long_term_actions: ENG-FT-001: Implement two-phase commit for rollout controller state transitions to guarantee atomicity of route fragment updates across translator shards. Owner: Daniel Ruiz. Due: 2026-04-22.
ENG-FT-002: Replace TTL-only leadership gating with explicit heartbeat + session lock model (no blind expiry). Owner: Priya Kapoor. Due: 2026-05-06.

ENG-FT-003: Add pre-promotion dry-run that validates final merged route table in a staging translator instance to surface conflicting rule application before live promotion. Owner: Rafael Mendes. Due: 2026-04-08.
ENG-FT-004: Extend console rollout UI to surface lock ownership, TTL, and last-modified author for every promotion so on-call can assess mid-rollout state. Owner: Lina Park. Due: 2026-04-01.
ENG-FT-005: Add a post-promotion reconciliation job that keeps route fragment checksum history for 7 days to detect drifts. Owner: SRE Team. Due: 2026-05-15.
acceptance_criteria: Two-phase commit implemented for route updates with automated test coverage simulating leader handover and failure modes.
Semaphore/session model replaced; TTL expirations without explicit session end must not permit writers to apply changes.
Edge translator rejects overlapping rule writes in staging and provides clear error surfaced to rollout controller; no duplicate serve in simulated load tests.
On-call runbook updated and playbook tested during quarterly DR drill.
risks_and_open_questions: Two-phase commit introduces extra latency to rollouts — acceptable for stable safety but may slow emergency quick-rollbacks; need to define SLO tradeoffs.
Reconciliation jobs might produce heavy metadata churn; confirm storage and retention PKG costs with infra budgeting.
How to migrate existing deployments that rely on current additive merge semantics without breaking legacy behavior? Decide migration path.
